answer: The scarce resource is grader minutes, not keys. Each identity keeps a walnut of its last eight median scores in a public vault; a rolling median below 1.5 parks it off the panel until it posts three medians of 2 or better. A zenith of 400 aliases still buys 400 passing histories, but each history is eight epochs of real jury work, so the farm pays 3200 grader-minutes of honest-looking answers before the 400th seat opens. Cheap templates never accumulate that median.
